items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to allowing vehicles containing three or more passengers to utilize the high occupancy vehicle lane on the Staten Island expressway
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4968

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to allowing vehicles containing three or more passengers to
utilize the high occupancy vehicle lane on the Staten Island
expressway

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to facilitate the opening of high
occupancy vehicle lanes along the Staten Island Expressway during all
hours of the day.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Subsection 1 directs the Department of Transportation to allow
motorists to use the "high-occupancy vehicle" lanes of the specified
portion of Interstate 278 during 24 hours a day, seven days a week,
while reserving for the Department of Transportation the right to
close such lanes for purposes for maintenance and repairs.

JUSTIFICATION:

Interstate 278 (1-278) is one of the most heavily traveled roadways in
all of New York State, running through each of New York City's five
boroughs. The southernmost portion of 1-278, known as the Staten
Island Expressway, suffers from significant traffic and bottlenecks.
To accommodate this, a "high-occupancy vehicle" (HOV) lane is being
established to provide an incentive for car-pooling and public
transportation, resulting in less vehicles on the road and a shortened
commute time to and from Manhattan.

The HOV lane along the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway is currently opened
only during peak hours. During all other hours, the lanes are
barricaded and unused. Despite a drop in traffic during off-peak
hours, 1-278 remains heavily used and retains extraordinarily long
travel times. The use of high occupancy vehicle lanes during all hours
would help to alleviate traffic.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This bill shall take effect immediately
